title: Add NUT-12 DLEQ verification
body:
This PR adds the capability to do DLEQ verification for ecash proofs after minting/swapping or before receiving from another user.
This allows a wallet to:
- Prevent tracking attempts from the mint
- Prevent fraudulent token redemption after receiving from a third party in general, or, in case of receiving locked ecash

See [NUT-12](https://github.com/cashubtc/nuts/blob/main/12.md)

title: Basic P2PK Send and Receive
body:
This PR adds functions and required parameters to send and receive tokens locked to a public key.
For now only inputs without spending conditions can be sent.
Locking proofs in a token supports basic SIG_INPUTS spending conditions.
This allows wallet applications to construct tokens that can be verified and received offline.

title: Refactor Library Interface for Flexibility and Extensibility
body:
This PR proposes changes to the library interface and overall structure to allow a user to either use the library's own types for `Mint`, `Proof`, etc. or define their own types and use them with static library functions as long as these types conform to protocols like `MintRepresenting` of `ProofRepresenting`.

As a consequence library functions can no longer be called on instances like this
`mint.receive(token)`
but instead need to be declared static, on `CashuSwift` as follows
`CashuSwift.receive(from: mint, token)`
to be able to accept generic inputs like protocols (`mint` is of type `MintRepresenting`).

This means a wallet like [macadamia](https://github.com/zeugmaster/macadamia) can declare types that have additional functionality and properties like database macros, while also allowing a user who does not require them to simply use the basic types CashuSwift provides.

As a result, some boilerplate `Codable` logic can also be removed and miscellaneous minor improvements be made.
